note: 8 of 13 items dated Nov 23-25 (last 24-48h), exceeding the 3-5 freshness minimum. Several source pages (247wallst, brecorder, invezz, forbes) returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch and could only be verified via search-engine snippets cross-checked against 2+ independent outlets each -- treat exact figures as directionally reliable. No major fresh SGX-developer-specific (property) headline found this run; the SGX section leans on banks and REITs only.

items.headline: Credit spreads blow out even as equities bounced -- confirms the 'no credit confirmation' warning
items.summary: US high-yield option-adjusted spreads widened from 323bp to 376bp between Nov 13-20, the largest one-week jump since early 2026; CCC-and-below spreads widened 92bp vs just 8bp for investment grade. A Nov 24 Forbes piece argues the bond market is flagging the equity rebound as unstable even as stocks rallied off Monday's Nvidia-driven surge.
items.actionable: Credit is the tell to watch before adding risk -- a book already overweight levered silver/miners and HK tech should treat the equity bounce as fragile and keep the cash pile as dry powder rather than chasing it.

items.headline: Core PCE + Q3 GDP revision due tonight (21:30 SGT), last clean inflation read before Dec 9 FOMC
items.summary: October core PCE is forecast at +0.3% m/m / 3.2% y/y (up from 3.1%), with Q3 GDP's second estimate seen at 3.5% (up from 3.4%); the Fed's Beige Book follows at 2pm ET. FOMC's Williams has said inflation remains 'too high' and signaled he favors another hike, while Governor Waller reportedly floated support for a larger 50bp move given hot price data.
items.actionable: A hot core-PCE print plus hawkish Fed-speak is the single biggest near-term threat to both gold/silver (real-rate pressure) and the HK-tech/SGX risk legs -- watch the 21:30 SGT release closely before SGX/HKEX open.

items.headline: Silver extends crash to ~$42, now ~65% below January's $121.65 peak; gold-silver ratio near 86
items.summary: Silver fell a further 2-3% on Nov 24 to roughly $42/oz (SLV closed $36.84, -5.32%), down ~65% from its January 2026 all-time high and down over 21% in the past month alone. The gold-to-silver ratio has blown out to ~85.8 from ~55 at the cycle peak, even as COMEX registered silver inventories sit over 70% below their 2021 peak -- a tension between apparent physical tightness and continued price collapse.
items.actionable: This is the live risk to the book's core position -- leveraged silver/miners exposure is still falling despite tight registered inventories, so this is not yet a buy-the-dip signal; size and margin cushion matter more than conviction right now.

items.headline: SEC accounting probe into Nvidia zeroes in on the 2025 geography-reporting change that erased Singapore
items.summary: Reuters sources say the SEC's investigation is focused on Nvidia's 2025 shift from billing-address to customer-headquarters revenue reporting, which eliminated Singapore as a separately disclosed market -- Singapore billings had been nearly half of global revenue under the old method. The probe also sits alongside separate concerns about 'circular' AI financing deals and revenue quality; Reuters could not confirm the probe's exact scope.
items.actionable: An open accounting probe into Nvidia's single biggest swing factor (AI capex) is a standing tail risk for HK tech names (Tencent, Alibaba, Xiaomi) that are themselves ramping AI capex on the same demand assumptions -- don't treat Monday's Nvidia-driven HK tech pop as durable.

items.headline: Bitcoin falls below $60,000, erasing Monday's Nvidia-rally spike; record $4.71bn November ETF outflows
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped roughly 2-3% on Nov 24 to near $59,700-60,200, giving back all of Monday's bounce tied to Nvidia's Jensen Huang reinstatement. US spot Bitcoin ETFs logged a fifth straight day of outflows, taking November's cumulative outflow to a record $4.71 billion.
items.actionable: Crypto trading 24/7 is the cleanest real-time read on whether Monday's risk rally has legs -- its full round-trip lower, alongside widening credit spreads, corroborates the 'rebound not confirmed' thesis and argues against deploying cash into the bounce.

items.headline: Hang Seng gives back Nvidia-rally gains, closes down 0.73%; Hang Seng Tech -1.17% as Xiaomi, Meituan slide
items.summary: Hong Kong stocks opened up over 1% on continued optimism from Nvidia's CEO reinstatement, with Hang Seng Tech briefly gaining 2%+ intraday, but both indices faded into the close -- HSI finished at 22,219.65 (-164pts) and Hang Seng Tech at 3,466.87. Xiaomi and Meituan each fell more than 3% as early AI enthusiasm gave way to property stress and demand concerns.
items.actionable: The intraday fade from +1% to a red close is itself the signal -- HK tech is trading as a high-beta Nvidia proxy rather than on its own fundamentals, so the book's HK tech sleeve stays exposed to further US AI-sentiment whiplash into tonight's PCE. Southbound money still bought the dip (+HK$6.2bn) even as the index fell.

items.headline: KOSPI surges 6.32% to reclaim 5,000 as Korea's foreign-selling streak finally breaks
items.summary: South Korea's KOSPI jumped 297.49 points (+6.32%) to 5,006.03 on Nov 24, a day behind the US's Nvidia-driven rally, ending foreign investors' 7-session net-selling streak (+₩739.2bn) and extending domestic institutional buying to a 2nd day (+₩869.2bn). Retail, which had bought every prior crash-day dip, flipped to a ₩2.04 trillion net sell -- selling into the rally rather than buying it.
items.actionable: Korea's belated catch-up rally, with foreign/institutional buying but retail selling into strength, is a reminder that Asia's AI-capex-linked markets (Samsung, SK Hynix) remain high-beta to the same Nvidia-sentiment swings driving the book's HK tech sleeve.

items.headline: Alibaba and Tencent earnings both show AI capex burning cash faster than it's generating profit
items.summary: Alibaba's Sept-quarter revenue rose 10% y/y to RMB271.5bn and beat consensus, but adjusted EPS missed and AI-infrastructure spend continued to outpace operating cash generation. Tencent's Q3 revenue rose 8% y/y to RMB207.3bn, but non-IFRS profit fell 6% y/y as R&D and new AI-initiative costs ate into margins.
items.actionable: Both core HK tech holdings are now explicitly trading off AI-capex-ROI narratives rather than core-business growth -- the same scrutiny now applied to Nvidia's accounting could extend to these names' own AI spend disclosures.

items.headline: S-REITs down ~14% YTD vs STI +12% as T-bill yields retreat from 4%+ peaks toward 2.5-3.0%
items.summary: The iEdge S-REIT Index was down about 14.1% YTD as of Nov 13 versus the Straits Times Index's 12.3% gain, a 33-point divergence driven by refinancing at higher rates. Singapore 6-month T-bill yields have fallen from above 4% to roughly 2.5-3.0%, which should reduce the competing-yield headwind that has weighed on REIT valuations.
items.actionable: Falling T-bill yields are the clearest tailwind building for the SGX REIT sleeve even as the sector remains deeply out of favor -- this is the most plausible near-term mean-reversion trade in the book if rate-cut expectations hold, but watch tonight's PCE/GDP for confirmation that yields keep falling.

items.headline: US warns China it has met only two-thirds of Busan rare-earth pledges as truce extension holds
items.summary: China extended its pause on expanded rare-earth export controls by two months (past the original Nov 10 expiry) as part of the Busan trade-truce implementation, with the US reciprocating by extending tariff exclusions on 178 Chinese products. However, US officials said Friday that Beijing has fulfilled only about two-thirds of its rare-earth commitments, keeping the truce's durability in question ahead of further talks.
items.actionable: The truce is holding but compliance gaps keep the China rare-earth leverage threat alive -- the watch-list basket (MP/Lynas/USAR) stays a binary political-headline trade rather than a fundamentals trade until the two-thirds compliance gap is resolved.

items.headline: Oil at 3-month lows on oversupply and US-Iran diplomacy, but Houthi attack claim and Goldman warning flag upside risk
items.summary: Brent and WTI both slipped to three-month lows on Nov 24 (Brent ~$89, WTI ~$80-82) as optimism built around US-Iran talks (VP Vance engaging Qatar as intermediary) and oversupply concerns ahead of this weekend's OPEC+ meeting, where Iraq has disputed OPEC+'s assessment of its production capacity. Yemen's Houthis claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh refinery (damage unconfirmed), and Goldman Sachs raised its December Brent forecast from $90 to $105, warning of a possible spike to $140 in 2027 if regional supply disruptions persist.
items.actionable: Oil is pricing diplomacy-driven calm, but the Houthi/Saudi and Iraq/OPEC+ frictions are live tail risks that could reprice energy and inflation expectations fast -- relevant mainly as an input to tonight's PCE read and any renewed stagflation narrative that would hurt both equities and the cash-heavy defensive stance.

items.headline: Ukraine escalates deep strikes on Russian oil infrastructure; Western intel warns of possible Russian nuclear ASAT move
items.summary: Ukraine struck three major Russian oil nodes over Nov 22-23 -- the Novoshakhtinsk refinery, Tatarstan's Kaleikino storage tanks, and the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez refinery roughly 1,449km from the border -- as part of an escalated deep-strike campaign. Separately, Western intelligence has warned of a potential Russian nuclear anti-satellite deployment, while Latvia's president said the war could reach a decisive tipping point in 2027.
items.actionable: Escalation in Russian energy-infrastructure strikes is a latent upside catalyst for oil and a tail-risk bid for gold/safe-havens -- a genuine escalation (vs. the market's current calm pricing) would be one of the few scenarios that could pull gold higher even as silver remains under separate liquidation pressure.
